title: Power Apps: responsive, multi-column starting layout for SharePoint list forms (preview)
summary: The roadmap facts, responsive layout behaviour and environment command are supported. Minor corrections should clarify the alternative maker role and existing platform billing, and resolve gaps between the governance text and controls table.

claims.claim: The change introduces a responsive, multi-column starting layout for new SharePoint custom forms.
claims.quote: The public preview of SharePoint Customize Forms introduces a responsive, multi-column starting layout for new forms in eligible commercial SharePoint tenants.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a public preview in eligible commercial SharePoint tenants.
claims.quote: The public preview of SharePoint Customize Forms introduces a responsive, multi-column starting layout for new forms in eligible commercial SharePoint tenants.

claims.claim: Makers can customise the forms while preserving their connection to SharePoint list actions.
claims.quote: Makers can customize these forms while preserving their connection to SharePoint list actions.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the responsive template's arrival default or tenant enablement mechanics.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Power Apps responsive multi-column forms template preview enable disable eligibility tenant setting default. Opened sharepoint-form-integration and list-tenantsettings; read roadmap. They do not state the arrival default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licensing requirement has been published for the new template's preview or General Availability.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps SharePoint customized responsive forms licensing preview standard connectors meter pay as you go; SharePoint custom forms Power Apps licensing nonpremium premium connectors Microsoft 365 responsive template. Opened feature, integration, licensing overview and licensing FAQ pages.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Understand SharePoint forms integration names no prerequisite licence for the layout.
claims.quote: Create and customize the form: Open your list in SharePoint or Microsoft Lists to customize its form.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The general integration overview lists a subscription to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: Prerequisites: A subscription to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform.

claims.claim: Some Microsoft 365 licences include limited Power Apps rights for Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.
claims.quote: Some Microsoft 365 licenses include limited Power Apps and Power Automate use rights. These use rights are intended for scenarios that use Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.

claims.claim: Standalone licensing provides premium capabilities beyond the limited Microsoft 365 rights.
claims.quote: For example, Power Apps Premium and Power Automate Premium provide premium capabilities for licensed users.

claims.claim: A particular form's licensing can depend on capabilities the maker adds.
claims.quote: The licenses and use rights that your organization needs depend on the products, features, data sources, and environments that you use.

claims.claim: No meter is documented for the new responsive layout at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps SharePoint customized responsive forms licensing preview standard connectors meter pay as you go. Opened sharepoint-form-integration, pricing-billing-skus and pay-as-you-go-meters. No separate layout meter; general Power Apps app metering is documented.
claims.fix: Narrow 'no meter is documented for this feature' to 'No separate meter is documented for the responsive layout; existing Power Apps billing rules still apply.' In the cost rationale, replace 'names no licence or meter' with 'names no layout-specific licence or meter'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pay-as-you-go-meters.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The previous template used a mobile-sized canvas.
claims.quote: The previous template used a mobile-sized canvas with a single-column form.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The previous template used a single-column form.
claims.quote: The previous template used a mobile-sized canvas with a single-column form.

claims.claim: The new template uses the Flexible canvas type.
claims.quote: The new template uses the Flexible canvas type and a responsive layout that adapts to the available space.

claims.claim: The responsive layout adapts to available space.
claims.quote: The new template uses the Flexible canvas type and a responsive layout that adapts to the available space.

claims.claim: Learn qualifies its template description as applying where the template is enabled for new form creation.
claims.quote: This article describes the responsive template where it's enabled for new form creation.

claims.claim: Existing customised forms are not automatically converted to the new layout.
claims.quote: Existing customized forms keep their current layout and aren't automatically converted.

claims.claim: Makers open a list and select Integrate > Power Apps > Customize forms.
claims.quote: 1. Open your list in SharePoint or Microsoft Lists. 2. Select Integrate > Power Apps > Customize forms.

claims.claim: The generated form uses one column below an app width of 640.
claims.quote: If(App.Width < 640, 1, If(App.Width < 900, 2, 3))

claims.claim: The generated form uses two columns at app widths from 640 to below 900.
claims.quote: 640 to less than 900. | Two.

claims.claim: The generated form uses three columns at app widths of 900 or more.
claims.quote: 900 or more. | Three.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: App-width breakpoints do not guarantee the number of columns that fit every SharePoint panel, so host testing is needed.
claims.quote: These app-width breakpoints don't guarantee how many columns fit inside every SharePoint panel. Check the form in its actual host, not only in Studio.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Generated SharePointIntegration actions connect the form to New, View, Edit, Save and Cancel list operations.
claims.quote: Preserve the generated actions so the nested form responds to the list's New, View, Edit, Save, and Cancel operations:

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn advises preserving the generated SharePointIntegration actions.
claims.quote: Preserve the containers' responsive sizing and the generated SharePointIntegration actions.

claims.claim: Learn advises retaining the form inside its layout containers and preserving responsive sizing formulas.
claims.quote: Keep the form inside its layout containers. Change the title, description, and fields without replacing responsive sizing formulas with fixed values.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The generated form's DataSource is the SharePoint list being customised, rather than a newly described data source.
claims.quote: The form's DataSource is the list you customize.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure and Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Users with at least Read or Restricted View access to the linked list inherit access to its customised form.
claims.quote: Any user who has at least Read or Restricted View access to the linked SharePoint list inherits access to the form.

claims.claim: Users granted permissions only to specific list items do not have access to the customised form.
claims.quote: Users who have only been given permissions to specific items in the list don't have access to the customized form.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor the feature's Learn page describes an identity change.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Power Apps responsive multi-column forms template preview enable disable eligibility tenant setting default. Read the roadmap and full sharepoint-form-integration page, including user access; neither describes an identity change.

claims.claim: No autonomous behaviour is described for the responsive template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive forms template enable disable PowerShell Power Platform API tenant settings Flexible canvas November 2026. Read roadmap and sharepoint-form-integration, including actions and background-event warning; no autonomous feature is described.

claims.claim: Learn warns against Launch() in SharePointIntegration properties because events can run while the form is hidden.
claims.quote: Don't use imperative functions such as Launch() in SharePointIntegration properties such as OnNew and OnView. These events can run in the background even when the form isn't visible.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Replacing generated card formulas based on Parent.NumberOfColumns with fixed values can stop fields reflowing.
claims.quote: Generated data cards use formulas based on Parent.NumberOfColumns for their position and width. Replacing those formulas with fixed values can stop fields from reflowing.

claims.claim: Power Apps currently has no automated method to copy a form between environments.
claims.quote: While you can manually copy a form from one environment to another, there's currently no automated method in Power Apps to copy a form from one environment to another.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn advises checking forms at each layout size.
claims.quote: Check long labels, multiline fields, required-field messages, and scrolling at each layout size.

claims.claim: Creating a custom SharePoint form creates a canvas app in the default environment unless a different form environment is designated.
claims.quote: When a maker creates a custom SharePoint form in SharePoint, it creates a canvas app in the default environment.

claims.claim: A separate environment can be designated to store new SharePoint custom forms.
claims.quote: Run the following PowerShell cmdlet to set the SharePoint form environment: Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment -EnvironmentName '<EnvironmentName>'

claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment -EnvironmentName '<EnvironmentName>' designates where newly created SharePoint custom forms are saved.
claims.quote:
Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment -EnvironmentName 'EnvironmentName'
This command designates the environment newly created SharePoint custom forms save to, instead of the default environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no Power Platform admin center UI path to designate the SharePoint custom form environment.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint custom form environment designate Power Platform admin center UI Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment. Opened powerapps-powershell, manage-default-environment and admin-manage-apps; all route designation through PowerShell.

claims.claim: Only tenant admins can call the environment-designation cmdlet.
claims.quote: Modifies which environment Power Platform users save Sharepoint form apps. Only tenant admins can call this command.

claims.claim: Only a production environment can be designated for SharePoint custom forms.
claims.quote: Only production environment can be designated for SharePoint custom forms.

claims.claim: Changing the designated environment does not automatically migrate existing forms.
claims.quote: Existing custom forms don't automatically migrate to the newly designated environment.

claims.claim: Deleting the designated environment deletes the custom forms stored there.
claims.quote: If the designated SharePoint custom form environment is deleted, the custom forms are deleted with it.

claims.claim: Learn says a user creating a custom form in a designated environment needs the Environment Maker role.
claims.quote: The ability for a user to create a custom form in a designated environment requires that user to have the Environment Maker role.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'The PowerShell overview says creators need Environment Maker, while Manage Power Apps documents the SharePoint custom form maker role as an alternative in a nondefault environment with Dataverse.' Both sources are already cited; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/admin-manage-apps explicitly accepts either role.

claims.claim: The SharePoint custom form maker role can restrict makers to creating and editing SharePoint custom forms in a nondefault environment.
claims.quote: Outside of the default environment, an admin can unassign the Environment Maker security role from users and assign the SharePoint custom form maker security role.

claims.claim: Distinguishing SharePoint custom form makers from general Environment Makers requires Dataverse in the environment.
claims.quote: The ability to distinguish SharePoint custom form makers from general Environment Makers requires Dataverse in the environment where the privilege is to be changed.

claims.claim: The environment-control pages discuss SharePoint custom forms generally without explicitly naming the new responsive template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive forms template enable disable PowerShell Power Platform API tenant settings Flexible canvas November 2026. Read powerapps-powershell designation section, admin-manage-apps and manage-default-environment; none names the responsive template.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin or maker switch to turn the new starting layout on or off or retain the previous template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Power Apps responsive multi-column forms template preview enable disable eligibility tenant setting default; SharePoint responsive forms template enable disable PowerShell Power Platform API tenant settings Flexible canvas November 2026. Opened feature and list-tenantsettings pages.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not defined how tenants become eligible for the responsive template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Power Apps responsive multi-column forms template preview enable disable eligibility tenant setting default. Read roadmap and sharepoint-form-integration; the former says eligible commercial tenants, and the latter says where enabled, without eligibility criteria.

claims.claim: The text reports an absent layout switch without representing that absence in the controls table.
claims.quote: Text: 'Microsoft has not documented a setting that turns the new starting layout on or off.' The sole table row is 'Environment where new SharePoint custom forms are saved'.
claims.fix: Remove the final sentence of Governance controls about the undocumented layout switch. Keep the existing question about retaining the previous template in Open questions; do not add a control row.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, second bullet
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to check generated actions and responsive formulas, but neither control appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Confirm that makers keep the generated SharePointIntegration actions and responsive container formulas when they edit forms.' The table contains only the form-environment control.
claims.fix: Remove the second At rollout bullet beginning 'Confirm that makers keep'. The existing What's changing and Why it matters paragraphs already carry the verified preservation guidance; do not add control rows.

controlChecks.governs: Environment where new SharePoint custom forms are saved
